name: seed_r2_readback
notes: ALU-seeding sanity: falu2i(unwritten+K) then direct store.

name: unwritten_reads_zero
notes: Sentinel-register sanity: r14 is never written by any case in this matrix; EXP-0087 MOVE-04 predicts it reads exactly 0.0.

name: positive_control_deliberate_mismatch
notes: Same construction as seed_r2_readback but an oracle chosen to be UNREACHABLE (30.0 != 999.0) -- proves match-detection actually detects mismatch, not a rubber stamp.

name: route_load_replicate_fail_route6
notes: EXACT replication of EXP-0099's own ROUTE_LOAD (route=6) construction: device_load with extmode=0 (its old, WRONG default) and dst_lo/dst_ext9 derived from the target register 7 via the old naive formula (the isa_helpers.device_load() convention every prior experiment used) -- reproduces the documented blocker before this experiment's own fix is applied.

name: fix_extmode_reg7_falu2
notes: THE decisive fix, same falu2 register-register shape as EXP-0099's own ROUTE_LOAD: extmode=2*7=14 (this experiment's own H1 formula), dst_lo/dst_ext9 held at the known-good token (1,1) instead of being derived from register 7. Directly reverses the preceding replicate case.

name: fix_extmode_reg7_falu2i
notes: Same fix, via falu2i (register + immediate) instead of falu2 (register-register) -- the form the compiler's own multiload census (analysis/census.py) actually emits, INCLUDING its mods=0xC0 tail field (the compiler's own v0/multiload anchors always emit mods in {0xC0,0x20,0x40,0x00,0xA0} depending on context; 0xC0 is what census_load_add.metal itself emits). K_SMALL added so a correct result requires REAL arithmetic on the loaded value, not merely a pass-through. A pilot-phase run of this EXACT case with isa_helpers' naive mods=0 DEFAULT failed (read K_SMALL alone, i.e. srcA read as 0) -- see the following adversarial case and PROGRESS.md Milestone 3.

name: adversarial_falu2i_mods_naive_default
notes: IDENTICAL to fix_extmode_reg7_falu2i except mods=0 (the naive isa_helpers.falu2i_raw() default, i.e. 'just don't set the field') instead of the compiler-observed 0xC0. Falsifies 'mods is don't-care once extmode/dst_lo/dst_ext9 are right': this pilot-phase discovery (mods bits 6 AND 7 must BOTH be set; either bit alone still fails, structurally the same shape as EXP-0090's own 'opflags must be 3, not 1' finding for falu2's two-real-operand form) is a THIRD required field for falu2i-consumed loads, on top of extmode and the dst_lo/dst_ext9 token.

name: fix_extmode_reg3
notes: Generalization: relocate the consumer register to r3 (a LOW register, unlike the r7 anchor) via extmode alone.

name: fix_extmode_reg16
notes: Generalization: relocate to r16, the first register requiring the FULL 7-bit srcA_reg field (beyond falu2's own 4-bit dst-nibble range) -- r15 deliberately avoided (that is R_IDX; loading into it would corrupt this same program's own addressing).

name: fix_extmode_reg20
notes: Generalization: relocate to r20, confirming the formula holds well past the low-register range every prior hand-built experiment (EXP-0090/EXP-0099) confined itself to.

name: adversarial_extmode_unchanged_srcA_mismatch
notes: extmode left at 0 (its correct value for target r0) but the consumer's srcA_reg set to 3 (mismatched) -- a plain field mismatch must fail; this is the mechanism, not 'route'.

name: adversarial_dstfields_naive_formula
notes: extmode CORRECTLY set (2*3=6) but dst_lo/dst_ext9 computed from the target register via the old naive formula (3,0) instead of being copied from the known-good token (1,1) -- falsifies 'derive dst_lo/dst_ext9 from the target register' as a repair strategy.

name: adversarial_dstfields_zero_extmode_correct
notes: extmode CORRECTLY set (2*3=6) but dst_lo/dst_ext9=(0,0) (an arbitrary, not-copied value) -- falsifies 'dst_lo/dst_ext9 is don't-care as long as extmode is right'.

name: adversarial_dstfields_zero_extmode_unchanged
notes: extmode left at 0 (its CORRECT value for target r0) but dst_lo/dst_ext9 changed away from the known-good token (1,1) to (0,0) -- falsifies 'dst_lo/dst_ext9 is universally don't-care'; even with extmode already correct, disturbing dst_lo/dst_ext9 alone breaks the load.

name: control_dst_nibble_independent_of_srcA
notes: Consumer reads r16 (low 4 bits = 0) but the ALU's OWN dst nibble is 8 (deliberately NOT matching r16's low bits) -- confirms falu2's dst nibble is an independent low-register (0-15) write target, not required to alias the source's low bits (an early pilot-phase over-theory this case exists to falsify; see PROGRESS.md Milestone 2).

name: move_replicate_baseline
notes: Replicates EXP-0099's own move_baseline_fail_replicate: falu2i writes V_LOW=30.0 to r2, reg_move(dst=3,src=2) -- predicted (per EXP-0099 + this experiment's own pilot) to read back the exact denormal bit pattern 0x00000100, not V_LOW.

name: move_producer_independence_altvalue
notes: SAME construction as move_replicate_baseline, but the producer writes a DIFFERENT value (V_ALT=2.0, not V_LOW=30.0) to r2 -- decisive: if reg_move genuinely read r2, this MUST differ from the baseline case. Predicting the IDENTICAL 0x00000100 output.

name: move_loadsourced_independence
notes: SAME reg_move, but r2 is written by a (this experiment's own H1 FIXED, genuinely working) device_load instead of falu2i -- extends producer-independence across producer FAMILY too, on a load path now independently proven functional (unlike EXP-0099's own analogous case, which used the pre-fix, non-working load).

name: move_srcreg_pair01_r0
notes: src_reg=0 (src_flag=0, GPR mode), unrelated to the producer register (r2) -- register-PAIR-quantization probe: predicts src_reg=0 and src_reg=1 read IDENTICAL content on this carrier.

name: move_srcreg_pair01_r1
notes: src_reg=1 (src_flag=0, GPR mode), unrelated to the producer register (r2) -- register-PAIR-quantization probe: predicts src_reg=0 and src_reg=1 read IDENTICAL content on this carrier.

name: move_srcreg_pair45_r4
notes: src_reg=4 -- second pair, a DIFFERENT stable value from the (0,1) pair and from the (2,3) pair's 0x00000100.

name: move_srcreg_pair45_r5
notes: src_reg=5 -- second pair, a DIFFERENT stable value from the (0,1) pair and from the (2,3) pair's 0x00000100.

name: move_srcreg_8_reads_zero
notes: src_reg=8 -- outside this carrier's populated preload region (matches EXP-0087 MOVE-04's 'far above range reads 0' pattern).

name: move_srcflag1_positive_control_1
notes: src_flag=1 (documented 'uniform/class' mode), src_reg=1 -- POSITIVE CONTROL: proves the harness and this instruction CAN read genuinely different, small, easily-distinguished content as src_reg varies (the literal integer 1 as raw bits) -- match-detection here is not a rubber stamp; the GPR-mode cases' producer-independence is a real finding, not a broken test.

name: move_srcflag1_positive_control_2
notes: src_flag=1 (documented 'uniform/class' mode), src_reg=2 -- POSITIVE CONTROL: proves the harness and this instruction CAN read genuinely different, small, easily-distinguished content as src_reg varies (the literal integer 2 as raw bits) -- match-detection here is not a rubber stamp; the GPR-mode cases' producer-independence is a real finding, not a broken test.

name: move_srcflag1_positive_control_3
notes: src_flag=1 (documented 'uniform/class' mode), src_reg=3 -- POSITIVE CONTROL: proves the harness and this instruction CAN read genuinely different, small, easily-distinguished content as src_reg varies (the literal integer 3 as raw bits) -- match-detection here is not a rubber stamp; the GPR-mode cases' producer-independence is a real finding, not a broken test.

name: move_srcclass_0x21_alu_sourced
notes: Retests EXP-0087's own open question (docs/isa/register-move-and-liveness.md section 1.3: byte+2=0x21, i.e. src_class=2, 'UNKNOWN -- do not rely on it') against a genuine ALU-computed r2=V_LOW=30 -- EXP-0087 could not distinguish 'real move' from 'lucky no-op' because its own carrier's r12 had no other writer. Here, if this were a real move it would read V_LOW=30.0; predicting it instead reads the SAME 0x00000100 as src_class=0 -- resolving the open question as 'reads the uniform file like src_class=0, not a real move' rather than leaving it UNKNOWN.

name: move_opdesc_sweep_zero
notes: op_desc=0 (byte+3), src_class=0 -- EXP-0087's own byte+2/op_desc sweep found nearly every non-(src_class=0,op_desc=8) combination is a silent zero; this extends that finding to op_desc specifically on an ALU-sourced (rather than EXP-0087's uniform-sourced) carrier.

name: positive_control_deliberate_mismatch_move
notes: Same construction as move_replicate_baseline but an oracle chosen to be UNREACHABLE -- proves match-detection for the MOVE_UNIFORM group specifically is not a rubber stamp either.
